es: Interpretar el lenguaje figurado y lo implícito en una letra breve: distinguir lo que dicen las palabras de lo que sugieren y justificar el tono con palabras concretas.

vocabulary.es: tocar la fibra, resonar en alguien

teaching.en: In song lyrics, figurative language works through metaphor: a paper boat on a grey river is never literal.
teaching.es: En las letras de canciones, el lenguaje figurado funciona mediante la metáfora: un barquito de papel en un río gris nunca es literal.
teaching.explanationEs: Lo literal es lo que dicen las palabras; lo figurado, lo que quieren decir. Una imagen imposible o rara suele pedir lectura figurada.

paper boat on a grey river is never literal.

teaching.en: To read between the lines, ask what the singer avoids saying, because the lyrics often imply more than any single verse states.
teaching.es: Para leer entre líneas, pregúntate qué evita decir la cantante, porque la letra suele dar a entender más de lo que afirma cualquier estrofa.
teaching.explanationEs: Imply: la letra sugiere algo que nunca dice con todas las letras; lo que se calla también comunica.

teaching.en: A hint of regret can sit inside a cheerful verse: the singer says I am fine, yet the tone quietly contradicts her.
teaching.es: Un matiz de pesar puede esconderse en una estrofa alegre: la cantante dice «estoy bien», pero el tono la contradice sin alzar la voz.
teaching.explanationEs: El tono (suave, irónico, resignado) se deduce de las palabras elegidas y de lo que no encaja con ellas.

teaching.en: A faint echo in an empty room can evoke absence, since a sound that returns without an answer suggests that someone has left.
teaching.es: Un eco tenue en una habitación vacía puede evocar ausencia, porque un sonido que vuelve sin respuesta sugiere que alguien se ha ido.
teaching.explanationEs: Un sonido o un espacio vacío insinúan una ausencia sin nombrarla.

sound that returns without an answer suggests that someone has left.

teaching.en: Understated lyrics may strike a chord because they never name the feeling: the listener supplies it, and the metaphor does the rest.
teaching.es: Una letra contenida puede tocar la fibra porque nunca nombra el sentimiento: lo pone el oyente y la metáfora hace el resto.
teaching.explanationEs: Understated = dicho con contención; el efecto emocional nace de lo que el oyente completa.

teaching.en: Separate what is literal from what is implied: a phone left face up beside the plate may suggest that someone is expecting a call.
teaching.es: Separa lo literal de lo implícito: un teléfono boca arriba junto al plato puede sugerir que alguien espera una llamada.
teaching.explanationEs: Interpretar es pasar del significado literal al oculto apoyándote en palabras concretas del texto.

prompt.es: ¿Qué significa, en sentido figurado, la imagen de la puerta?

choices.text: A promised talk that keeps failing to happen.
A real door that the singer has no key for.
A talk that she keeps postponing on purpose.

feedback.es: Un mañana convertido en puerta cerrada representa una conversación prometida que nunca llega; la cantante es quien llama, no quien la aplaza.

hint.es: Piensa en qué representa «mañana» cuando alguien lo promete y no lo cumple.

origin.text: You promised we would talk tomorrow, but tomorrow is a locked door, and I am tired of knocking.

prompt.es: Completa: «La letra da a entender que ella espera que él regrese.»

feedback.es: Imply es el verbo de lo que una letra sugiere sin decirlo; con lyrics (plural) va sin -s.

hint.es: El sujeto es plural (the lyrics): el verbo no lleva -s.

origin.text: The singer never says that she misses him. Instead she mentions the coat she keeps on the hook, and the lyrics ___ that she is still hoping he will come back.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Lee entre líneas antes de decidir qué quiere decir.»

answer.text: Read between the lines before you decide what she means
accepted: Read between the lines before you decide what she means
Before you decide what she means, read between the lines

feedback.es: La instrucción pone la lectura entre líneas antes de la conclusión: before you decide.

hint.es: Empieza por el verbo de lectura; before introduce lo que haces después.

prompt.es: ¿Qué da a entender el último verso de este fragmento?

choices.text: That she is afraid of sleeping alone in the dark.
That she still expects the other person to come back.
That she is proud of how well she keeps the house.

feedback.es: Dejar la luz encendida cada tarde, tras un eco en una sala antes ruidosa, sugiere que sigue esperando a alguien; el miedo a la oscuridad no aparece.

origin.text: Your name is a faint echo in a room that used to be loud, and every evening I still leave the light on in the hall.

prompt.es: Escucha al presentador y elige qué efecto logra la palabra «only» en el verso.

choices.text: It shows that the singer is losing patience with the bus company.
It signals that she is joking at her own expense.
It plays the complaint down and gives the verse a patient tone.

feedback.es: El presentador explica que only reduce la queja a propósito: el efecto es un tono paciente, no una protesta.

origin.audio: A radio presenter introduces the second verse of Last Bus Home. The singer says that she is not angry, only learning how long the last bus takes to come. The presenter points out that the word only makes the complaint smaller on purpose, so that the listener senses patience rather than anger.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada imagen de la letra con la idea que sugiere.

pairs.es: Un esfuerzo que no conduce a nada

pairs: My plans are water in my hands

pairs.es: Sus planes se le escapan sin que pueda retenerlos

pairs: Your laugh is a lamp in my kitchen

pairs.es: Su risa ilumina y da calor a la casa

pairs: I wear the silence like a coat

pairs.es: Se protege de todo con su silencio

feedback.es: Cada imagen dice una cosa y significa otra: el sentido figurado no se deduce palabra por palabra.

prompt.es: Escucha el comentario y elige qué sugiere el verso final sobre la cantante.

choices.text: She has accepted the ending, although a small hope remains.
She has lost all hope and wants to forget the person who left.
She feels relieved, because this verse is shorter and quieter than the others.
She is hopeful, because the unlocked door shows that she expects a reunion soon.

feedback.es: El final suena más callado y definitivo, pero la puerta sin cerrar indica que no ha renunciado del todo: aceptación con una esperanza pequeña.

origin.audio: The final verse of Last Bus Home is only four lines long. The singer folds a timetable into her pocket, turns off the hall light and says, to the empty hall, that some doors are better left unlocked. Nothing in the verse mentions the person who left. Critics have noticed that the word tomorrow appears in every verse except this one, and that its absence makes the ending feel quieter, less hopeful and more final. Yet the unlocked door suggests that the singer has not entirely given up. It is, the host concludes, a song that refuses to explain itself, and that is exactly why people keep arguing about it.

prompt.es: ¿Con qué propósito escribe el crítico este párrafo?

choices.text: To argue that the singer hides her real anger behind plain language.
To propose a less obvious reading than the one most listeners favour.
To complain that the singer never explains why the couple split up.
To compare the song with other songs about the weather.

feedback.es: El crítico contrasta la lectura habitual (una canción triste sobre una ruptura) con la suya (paciencia más que pérdida): propone una interpretación menos evidente.

origin.text: Some listeners hear Last Bus Home as a sad song about a break-up. I hear something less obvious: the singer never blames anyone, and the simple language she uses keeps the feeling in check. Sadness, here, is handled like weather: noticed, described, accepted. It is a song about patience more than loss.

prompt.es: Completa: «La canción no nombra el sentimiento, pero toca la fibra de quien esperó.»

feedback.es: Strike a chord es la colocación para algo que resuena en el oyente porque reconoce su propia experiencia.

origin.text: The song never names the feeling it describes, yet it seems to ___ a chord with anyone who has ever waited for a person who did not come.

prompt.es: Interpreta el verso: di qué dice literalmente y qué sugiere.

answer.text: Literally, she leaves a light on outside her house after the last bus has passed. The lyrics imply that she is still waiting for someone to come home, and the tone is patient rather than bitter.
accepted: Literally, she leaves a light on outside her house after the last bus has passed. The lyrics imply that she is still waiting for someone to come home, and the tone is patient rather than bitter.
The literal meaning is that she keeps the porch light on late at night. The verse suggests that she still hopes the person will return, and the tone is gentle rather than angry.

feedback.es: Una buena interpretación separa lo literal (la luz del porche) de lo implícito (la espera) y apunta el tono.

origin.text: Verso de «Last Bus Home»: «I leave the porch light burning, though the last bus has long gone by.» Escribe dos frases: una sobre lo literal y otra sobre lo que la letra da a entender.

prompt.es: ¿Qué tono domina en este verso de «Last Bus Home»?

choices.text: Angry, because she sends the letters away to hurt him.
Playful, because she treats the letters as a game.
Calm and almost practical about letting the past go.
Cold, because she feels nothing about the letters.

feedback.es: La cantante niega la ira («not anger») y describe el gesto como tareas de casa: el tono es sereno y casi práctico.

origin.text: Third verse of Last Bus Home: I fold your letters into paper boats and send them down the drain, one by one. It is not anger, love, it is only cleaning: some rivers have to be allowed to run.

prompt.es: Ordena: «El tono del verso deja ver un pesar silencioso.»

answer.text: The tone of the verse hints at quiet regret

feedback.es: Hints at + sustantivo expresa lo que el tono deja ver sin decirlo abiertamente.

prompt.es: Completa: «Nadie debería tomar esa línea al pie de la letra.»

feedback.es: Literally significa «al pie de la letra»: la línea es una metáfora, no una descripción real.

origin.text: When the singer says her heart is a suitcase, nobody should take the line ___. She does not own any luggage; she is telling us that she carries many memories.
